BARTOSZ NOWAK
bartosz.nowak@mail.example | +358 00 000 0019 | Helsinki

EXPERIENCE

Signal Processing Engineer
Polaris RF Labs, Helsinki | March 2020 -- present
(Career break September 2022 -- August 2023; see below)

- Write embedded C firmware for a 16-channel digital receiver module used in the company's ground-based surveillance radar product line, handling channelisation and decimation on a Xilinx Zynq SoC.
- Built and maintain the Python-based production test and calibration tooling (pytest, Jenkins CI) for factory acceptance testing of radar receiver boards; the suite runs nightly and catches hardware regressions before boards ship.
- My undergraduate EE training at Credit River University included a strong signals-and-systems foundation that I apply daily in filter design and spectral analysis work.
- Contributed to Polaris's work package on the LINKSAT-2 satellite programme, developing signal conditioning algorithms for a LEO communication payload prototype. Worked to EORA interface requirements and attended design reviews at ETEC.
- Since returning from my study break I have been coordinating a three-person sub-team responsible for calibration and test software. I assign tasks, run weekly standups, and review merge requests.
- All internal documentation, design reviews, and customer deliverables at Polaris are produced in English; I am the primary author of our external API documentation and have presented at two customer integration workshops.
- Employed in Finland on an EU Blue Card since 2020, renewed 2024.

Career Break
September 2022 -- August 2023
Took a year for further study, focusing on machine learning and software engineering courses. Returned to Polaris RF Labs in September 2023.

EDUCATION

B.A.Sc. Electrical Engineering
Credit River University | 2019
Focus: signals and systems, communications, digital electronics

PROJECTS

AuroraArray Phased-Array Demonstrator (Polaris RF Labs, 2024)
Designed and validated a 64-element L-band phased-array receive aperture for a ground-based interference monitoring system. Implemented digital beamforming in firmware (C on Zynq) and verified array patterns against simulated predictions. Responsible for the full signal chain from element-level digitisation through spatial filtering.

VHF Antenna Characterisation Campaign (Polaris RF Labs, 2021)
Led RF measurement of a VHF antenna array at the Sodankyla test range. Used a Keysight PNA-X network analyser for S-parameter characterisation and a near-field scanner for radiation pattern verification. Produced the measurement uncertainty analysis for the final qualification report.

SKILLS

Languages: Polish (native), English (professional working), Finnish (basic -- A2)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Polaris RF Labs in Helsinki has given me four years of hands-on work across the signal processing chain: embedded C firmware for digital receivers, production Python test infrastructure, phased-array beamforming validation, and signal conditioning for a satellite communication payload. I am writing to Kaikuvaara because the Senior Signal Processing Engineer role looks like it would channel that breadth into systems with real mission weight behind them, and the company's profile -- Finnish-based, genuine space heritage, serious RF instrumentation -- matches what I have been looking for.

My work at Polaris has ranged widely. I started writing channelisation firmware in C for a 16-channel digital receiver on a Xilinx Zynq SoC and building the Python-based factory acceptance test suite that still runs every night against our production receiver boards. My EE degree from Toronto is the foundation I draw on daily for filter design and spectral analysis. Since coming back from a study break in 2023 I have been coordinating a three-person sub-team responsible for calibration and test software, running standups and reviewing merge requests alongside my own technical deliverables. I have also led an RF measurement campaign at the Sodankyla VHF test range and contributed signal conditioning work for a LEO payload prototype under the LINKSAT-2 satellite programme. All of it in an English working environment -- I am the primary author of our customer-facing API documentation and have presented at integration workshops. The range has been good, but what I want now is sustained depth on one programme rather than constant breadth across many.

I should address the career gap. I took 2022--2023 off for further study, primarily machine learning and software engineering courses through open university programmes. It was a planned decision, not a crisis. I returned to Polaris a more effective engineer, particularly in how I think about automated testing and data pipelines, and I make no attempt to hide the gap.

On location: I have been in Helsinki since 2020 with no strong ties to the city beyond the current job. Oulu would be a straightforward relocation for me. I know the area from work trips to the Sodankyla test range, and the concentration of RF and sensor engineering in the region is part of the appeal. My EU Blue Card is renewed through 2026 and I have been continuously employed in Finland since 2020, so work authorisation is not a complication.

What I bring is someone who has built working systems across most of the RF signal processing stack and writes production code in both C and Python. The path has not been linear -- a Canadian EE degree, a study break, a broad role at Polaris -- but the result is an engineer who connects the pieces of a system. I would welcome the chance to discuss the role.

Bartosz Nowak

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
